title: The Orbit of Halcyon Drift
premise: August Winterbourne pilots the freighter Halcyon Drift along a dead trade route, ferrying cargo and avoiding the cryo-bay in the hold where three thousand colonists sleep in legal limbo—backups of lives the colonies abandoned. When a manifest audit flags his own name aboard a ship that was never registered to fly, August learns the sleeping passengers are scheduled for forced 'reclamation': their bodies harvested, their memories wiped into a colonial archive. With a stowaway archivist named Ione and a ragtag crew he never meant to love, August must outrun the Reclamation Authority, confront the truth that he is himself a backup who fled his original, and choose between waking the sleepers on a hostile world or preserving the archive that holds every erased memory of humanity. In the end, he wakes them at the cost of his own stored memories, becoming a stranger his found family must choose to love again.
about_author: Edmund Montrose is the pen name of a former merchant marine radio officer who spent eleven years on deep-route freighters before turning to fiction. He writes from a coastal town in Maine, where he claims the fog reminds him of shipboard watch rotations.

chapters.title: The Long Quiet
chapters.summary: August navigates the Halcyon Drift through a silent relay corridor, establishing his routine, his loneliness, and his careful avoidance of the cryo-hold. POV: August. Emotional beat: numb competence masking dread; the reader feels the weight of what he refuses to look at.

chapters.title: Manifest Anomaly
chapters.summary: A routine customs ping returns an impossible document: August's name listed as passenger one on the Meridian Rose, a vessel with no flight history. He assumes forgery. POV: August. Emotional beat: first crack in his invisibility; paranoia begins its slow bloom.

chapters.title: The Stowaway in Deck Nine
chapters.summary: August discovers Ione Vasquez hiding among water reclamation tanks—an archivist fleeing the Reclamation Authority with stolen index keys. Instead of spacing her, he feeds her. POV: alternating August/Ione. Emotional beat: reluctant mercy; two fugitives recognizing each other's fear.

chapters.title: What Sleeps Below
chapters.summary: Ione reveals the sleepers' fate: bodies reclaimed, memories archived, identities dissolved. August finally enters the cryo-bay and reads the nameplates. POV: August. Emotional beat: grief for strangers; the hold becomes a graveyard he can no longer ignore.

chapters.title: Crew of Convenience
chapters.summary: Engineer Tam Okafor and cook-surgeon Bex Lune learn the truth and vote—informally, over bad coffee—to keep flying rather than surrender. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: the fragile birth of found family; loyalty chosen before it is earned.

chapters.title: The Meridian Rose
chapters.summary: Ione decodes the ghost manifest: the Meridian Rose was the transport that carried August's original body—and the Authority believes a copy is walking free. POV: Ione. Emotional beat: betrayal of self; August learns he is the anomaly, not the victim of one.

chapters.title: Copy of a Man
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter: August's awakening in a backup facility seven years ago, his escape, and the memory he buried—that he chose to run rather than be decommissioned. POV: August (past). Emotional beat: shame confronted; the reader re-reads everything that came before.

chapters.title: Port of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: The crew docks at Ceres Verge to resupply and finds Reclamation officers scanning every berth. A dockhand they've never met lies for them. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: kindness from strangers; the cost of being known begins to outweigh the safety of anonymity.

chapters.title: Hunt Pattern Kestrel
chapters.summary: Authority hunter-ship Vantage locks onto the Drift's signature. A tense chase through debris fields ends with hull damage and Tam's arm crushed. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: survival has a price tag and it is being itemized.

chapters.title: Bex's Ledger
chapters.summary: While Tam heals, Bex confesses she once worked Reclamation intake and signed the order that froze the sleepers. The family fractures. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: guilt as inheritance; forgiveness withheld but not refused.

chapters.title: The Archive Key
chapters.summary: Ione's stolen keys prove she isn't a thief—she's the archive's designer, trying to undo her own creation. She proposes waking the sleepers on the unclaimed world Halcyon itself. POV: Ione. Emotional beat: redemption offered, not yet accepted; hope arrives dressed as a plan.

chapters.title: Interrogation of Ghosts
chapters.summary: August transmits to the Authority pretending to be his own original, buying time by exploiting their bureaucratic terror of copies. POV: August. Emotional beat: cunning as self-loathing; he performs the man he was supposed to be.

chapters.title: Course to Nowhere
chapters.summary: The Drift burns toward Halcyon, a storm-wrapped world with breathable air and no owners. Rations tighten; tempers fray; Ione and August grow close over navigation charts. POV: August. Emotional beat: tenderness inside desperation; the route becomes a home.

chapters.title: Vantage Closes
chapters.summary: The hunter ship corners them at a gravity well. To escape, August must slingshot through radiation that will fry the cryo-pods' failsafes—waking everyone early or killing them. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: impossible arithmetic; every option costs someone everything.

chapters.title: Three Thousand Heartbeats
chapters.summary: They thread the well. Pods survive at 40% integrity; sleepers begin waking in waves across days. The ship becomes a crowded, frightened village. POV: Bex. Emotional beat: chaos transformed into community; the hold becomes a hearth.

chapters.title: The First Woken
chapters.summary: Among the awakened is Mara Winterbourne—August's original's sister—who recognizes his face and calls him by a dead man's name. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: being seen without consent; identity as something others carry too.

chapters.title: Reckoning in the Galley
chapters.summary: Mara, Bex, and August collide over guilt, memory, and who owes whom. Ione mediates. The family nearly breaks, then chooses to hold. POV: August. Emotional beat: the price of survival made personal; confession without absolution.

chapters.title: Boarding Party
chapters.summary: Vantage catches them in orbit above Halcyon. Authority marines board; Tam seals decks, Bex triages wounds, Ione broadcasts the archive publicly so erasure becomes impossible. POV: Ione. Emotional beat: sacrifice distributed; courage as a group act.

chapters.title: Which Half Wakes
chapters.summary: Cornered in the cryo-bay, August faces the Authority's offer: surrender the sleepers' bodies and keep his freedom. He refuses, triggering full wake-cycle and overloading the archive uplink with every sleeper's memories at once. POV: August. Emotional beat: climax—the choice that defines him, made at maximum cost.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: The overload wipes August's stored backup-memories—his original life, his sister's childhood, his own name's origin. He wakes knowing only the last seven years. Mara tells him who he was. POV: Mara. Emotional beat: grief and gift entwined; memory surrendered so others could keep theirs.

chapters.title: Groundfall
chapters.summary: The Authority withdraws, scandalized by the public archive. The crew and three thousand settlers descend to Halcyon's surface and raise the first shelters in the rain. POV: Tam. Emotional beat: exhaustion transfigured into arrival; survival finally paying out.

chapters.title: The Orbit of Halcyon Drift
chapters.summary: Months later, the refitted Drift runs supply loops above the colony. August, still missing pieces, asks Bex whether you can love someone who doesn't remember loving you. She hands him a cup of coffee and says yes. POV: August. Emotional beat: resolution—found family as the memory that chooses to persist.
